problems.problem: BLOCKING — `capy edit --web` has no exit on the most common path. I drove the real page: `serveSecretTable` with rows that carry no `dirty` flag (which is what `editCommand.ts` always passes on the first render) renders NO way out. Buttons on a clean table are only ["Key","Value","Status","Updated","copy"] — the "Review N change" control only exists when a row is already dirty. Keyboard is dead too: dispatching `q`, `Escape`, `c` and `x` posted nothing (instrumented `window.fetch` recorded `[]`). The only way the flow ends is the wizard's 5-minute timeout, and `runSecretEditorInBrowser` never catches it, so the promise rejects with `CapyError: Timed out waiting for the browser (5 minutes).` — verified, settled value was exactly that. So: open `capy edit --web`, look at the table, reveal a value, close the tab → the CLI hangs five minutes and then EXITS WITH AN ERROR. The terminal's `q` quits instantly. Cancelling the value editor loops straight back into the same dead end. The e2e fixture hides this: `EDIT_ROWS[1]` is hand-set `dirty: true` with the comment "so the table offers the review stop" — the one state production never starts in. This is precisely the class of defect the browser-test rule exists to catch, and it was not caught.

`capy edit --web` and `capy decrypt --web` are unreachable from argv. `.command('edit').action(async () => { ... await cmd.execute(); })` (line 123) and `.command('decrypt').action(async () => { ... await cmd.execute(); })` (line 636) pass no options at all, and neither declares `--no-open`. Two of the parcel's three converted commands are dead code from the CLI's point of view — the only way to reach them is by importing the class. The report discloses this and points at `src/index.ts` not being its parcel, which is fair (no parcel owns it), but the consequence stands: this flow has never been run as a command, only as a library, and finding #1 above is what falls out of that. `capy add --web` IS reachable (`merged.web`) and is fine.

`showDecryptResult` leaves the process alive for two minutes. `ScreenServer.start()` binds a listening socket and its own timeout is `unref()`d, but the socket is not — so once `DecryptCommand.execute` returns, nothing exits until the result page is fetched or the 120s ScreenServer timeout fires. Measured directly: `showDecryptResult returned at 4 ms` … `PROCESS EXITED after 120007ms`. Any run where the page is not opened (`CAPY_WEB_NO_OPEN`, a `--no-open` equivalent, a headless agent, a browser launch that fails silently — `open()` is best-effort in a `try{}catch{}`) hangs `capy decrypt --web` for two minutes AFTER it has already written the plaintext file and printed the result. Nothing in the branch tests `showDecryptResult` at all.

The trainstop rail is built by the CLI (good — `src/core/secretEditPlan.ts` is a proper pure `branchCreatePlan`-style builder) but is only ever built ONCE, for `view: 'table'`. `serveSecretTable` calls `buildSecretTableData(p, nonce)` in `renderFirst` and never re-renders, so the `view` parameter's `'confirm-commit'`/`'cancelled'`/`'done'` branches — and with them roughly half of `secretEditPlan` (`answer`, `discarded`→`skipped`, the `result`-is-current case) — are exercised by unit tests and by nothing else. Verified in a browser: after clicking through to the review view the rail still reads `Step 1 of 4 / ● Edit values / 1 variable / ← you are here`, while the page beside it says "Review changes / This pushes to everyone". The rail lies on every stop after the first. The report discloses this as a packages/ui gap (`secret-table` moves `view` locally and does not re-request), which is accurate as a cause, but the user-visible effect is a stale "you are here" — the exact defect the trainstop work exists to remove.

The integration that actually is `capy edit --web` is untested. The ten new browser tests drive `serveSecretTable` and `serveSecretValueEditor` as separate one-shot servers; `runSecretEditorInBrowser` — the loop `editCommand.ts` calls, which stitches table → editor → table → commit across three separate loopback servers and three browser tabs — has no test at all, and it does not forward `onListen`, so it has no test seam either (I had to intercept `console.log` to get its URLs). I built that test myself and the happy path DOES work end to end (table → edit → editor save → table → Review → commit reaches `saveLocalEdits` with `{STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: 'sk_live_rotated'}`), so this is a coverage gap rather than breakage — but it is the gap that let finding #1 through.

Each `runBrowserWizard` call registers a `process.once('SIGINT')` that is never removed when the promise resolves normally. Pre-existing, but this parcel is the first caller to invoke it in a loop — `runSecretEditorInBrowser` costs two wizards per edit. Measured: SIGINT listener count grows 2 → 13 over 12 sequential wizards, unbounded. Separately, `browserWizard.ts` is outside the parcel's declared file list; the additions (`routes`, the `{ body }` decision) are additive, correctly guarded by the same Host/Origin/nonce/body-cap path, and the reference commit also edited this file — but it is now a merge-conflict magnet across eight parallel branches.

One cold run of the file gave 20 pass / 1 fail; seven subsequent runs were 21/21 and I could not reproduce it. Most likely first-run transpile + browser-launch cost against the 5s budget in `until()` (200 × 25ms). Worth a wider poll budget before this lands in CI.

`capy add --web`'s overwrite consent is downgraded rather than carried across. In the terminal it is an `inquirer` confirm defaulting to NO that aborts before anything opens; in `--web` the same sentence is concatenated into `reason`, which `SecretIntakeData` documents as "Short note shown above the form. Display only." I confirmed in a browser that the sentence renders and that the intake screen offers no cancel control at all (buttons: ["show","+ add another variable","Save & sync","copy"]), so "refusing" means closing the tab and waiting out a 5-minute timeout that then throws. Better than the old behaviour (which skipped the confirm entirely and overwrote in silence) and the wording is verbatim, so this is a real improvement — but a display-only note is not the same gate.

TRAINSTOPS ARE BUILT BY THE COMMAND: `src/core/secretEditPlan.ts` and `src/core/decryptPlan.ts` are pure, `branchCreatePlan`-shaped, single-cursor (`stateFor`) so two "you are here" markers are impossible — the defect is that `serveSecretTable` only calls the builder once, see the stale-rail finding. FILES OUTSIDE THE PARCEL: only `src/ui/browserWizard.ts` (shared, unowned, additive, same precedent as the reference commit). NOTHING under `src/ui/screens/` changed — `git diff --stat 25e8f61..HEAD -- src/ui/screens/` is empty, so packages/ui output is untouched and the three screen changes it wanted are reported, not made. `exportCommand.ts` correctly untouched. `intakePage.ts` + its test deleted with no remaining importers anywhere in the monorepo. VERDICT IS FAIL on the strength of the first finding alone: the parcel's headline flow cannot be completed by a user who does not edit something, and it fails by hanging for five minutes and then erroring. That state was never clicked because the e2e fixture pre-marks a row `dirty`.
